summary.whatChanges: Makes `safeParse`/`safeParseAsync` build their `ZodError` lazily: failed results expose `error` via a memoizing getter/setter, so issue finalization and error construction only happen on first read. Standard Schema `validate` now runs the schema directly, finalizing issues without a ZodError, and turns a synchronously throwing check into a rejected promise. Bundle-size ceilings raised.
behaviorChanges: Failed safeParse results no longer construct a ZodError until `.error` is read; custom/global error maps now run at read time, not parse time
The error instance is built once and cached; `result.error` can also be assigned to
`~standard.validate` with a check that throws synchronously now returns a rejected Promise instead of throwing synchronously
Standard Schema failures are produced by running the schema directly and finalizing raw issues, bypassing the previous IssueBag/safeParse path
Allowed gzipped bundle sizes for zod/mini fixtures raised by roughly 33–37 bytes each
risks: Error maps and issue finalization now run lazily, so side-effecting or config-dependent maps observe different timing/state (tests had to explicitly read `.error` to trigger them)
The failure result is no longer a plain object: the `error` getter fires on spread, clone, or serialization, and errors thrown during finalization now surface at read sites instead of at parse
In `standardProps.validate` a synchronous throw is swallowed and the schema is re-run asynchronously, so side-effecting checks can execute twice
`_safeParse` dropped the `_Err ?? $ZodError` fallback, so passing no error class now throws when the error is read
